$description: Foundation tokens v1.0: the single source. Generates CSS custom properties, a Jetpack Compose theme and a SwiftUI theme. Conforms to the Design Tokens Format Module 2025.10: every token carries a $type it owns or inherits from its group, dimensions and durations use the object form, colours use the object form with an explicit colour space, and typography line heights are unitless multipliers of the font size. Names are camelCase at every leaf; a generator lower-kebabs the path for CSS and camel-joins it for Kotlin and Swift, with no exceptions to code by hand.

bothdecks.product.$description: Two strings that may never be written as a literal in a design file: the product name and the taxonomy version. The name is not carried here. It has one home, the application identity, and a design file binds its variable from that value at import time rather than holding a second copy; a token file holding it would be exactly the duplicate the decision record exists to prevent. The placeholder is what a design or a template writes instead.

bothdecks.localeFormatting.$description: Where the product deliberately departs from the platform's own formatting symbols, and why. An entry is legitimate only when the shipped face genuinely cannot draw the platform's character: the test refuses a declaration whose original the face does carry, so this list cannot quietly become an excuse. Anything not declared here is taken from the platform, unexamined and unmodified.

substitutions.reason: The shipped text face carries no narrow no-break space, and neither does any open-licence tri-script variable sans without a reserved font name that was measured: Commissioner, Geologica and Manrope all lack it, and the one candidate that has it draws four Greek letters out of fifty-seven. The group separator in French numbers is therefore the no-break space the face does carry, rather than a formatting character drawn by a face nobody chose.

bothdecks.focusRing.$description: Which focus token every painted surface takes. The ring is 2 px (borderWidth.focus) with a 2 px outward offset, 3 px on cards, and is never drawn inset. A surface absent from this map has no declared ring and must not receive focusable content until it is added here. Every entry is held to 3:1 against its surface by the token test.

bothdecks.composition.$description: The pairs the design actually composes, with the WCAG 2.2 threshold each is held to. This is the input to the contrast test: a foreground that is not listed against a surface is not painted there, and a surface that is painted must appear here, in both themes. It is deliberately narrower than the cross product of every role, because a table that measures pairs nobody paints is not a stricter table, only a longer one - and it is deliberately wider than the surfaces alone, because surface.inverse and every fill are surfaces the design paints controls on.
bothdecks.composition.fullBleedNote: match.fill and surface.inverse are painted as whole surfaces, never as a mark laid on another surface, so they are measured as backgrounds and not as graphical objects. Anything drawn on them is listed in onFillPairs, graphicalPairs or the focusRing map.

surfaceSeparation.note: Three ways two surfaces are told apart, and each pair declares which one it uses. A pair under colourSeparated has nothing but its colour to do it and must clear the minimum. A pair under elevationSeparated is told apart by the named shadow, which must be non-zero in both themes; those two may share a colour, and in the light theme surface.raised is written as an alias of surface.card because the card already sits on the lightest step of the ramp. A pair under borderSeparated is told apart by the named border, which must clear boundaryMinimum against both surfaces: that is the 3:1 a non-text boundary owes a reader, and it is a stricter thing to ask than a faint difference of fill. A well is drawn this way on purpose. Its fill sits a hair off the surface so a form does not read as a grid of grey boxes, and its edge does the telling.

bothdecks.reducedMotion.$description: Which duration replaces which when the platform reports reduced motion. Emitted as data to all three targets so no platform has to remember the mapping. instant is already shorter than reduced and is left alone: raising it would make a reduced transition slower, which is the wrong direction. Springs are replaced by their own reducedDuration.
bothdecks.reducedMotion.rule: The reduced path must never take longer than the full path. The confirmation ribbon keeps its full confirmHold, overlapping the incoming card rather than being serialised in front of it, so the release-to-next-card cost is the same in both paths.

bothdecks.haptic.$description: Eight events, six of which vibrate. One pulse per event on both platforms; there are no composed patterns. Haptics are emitted to Kotlin and Swift, the only two targets that can fire them. When system haptics are off every haptic is off, with no exception: the blocking error carries its whole meaning in the visual and in the screen-reader announcement, as it must for anyone who never had haptics.

thresholdCrossed.note: Confirms that the gesture is armed, in both directions. The outcome is distinguished at release, not here.

bothdecks.platform.$description: Platform mechanisms the token format cannot express as values, carried as data so every generator emits the same thing.

themeSelection.rule: The platform's own setting selects the theme; an explicit choice overrides it.
themeSelection.css: Emit the light roles on :root, repeat the dark roles inside @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) guarded as :root:not([data-theme="light"]), and repeat them again under :root[data-theme="dark"] so an explicit choice wins in both directions.
themeSelection.compose: isSystemInDarkTheme() as the default, overridable by an explicit app setting.
themeSelection.swiftui: @Environment(\.colorScheme) as the default, overridable by an explicit app setting.

safeArea.rule: Safe-area insets are read from the platform at run time and are never written as a constant. No layout may carry a fixed inset value.

fonts.rule: Self-hosted only. No @import and no url() to another origin, for data protection. A family declares the files that carry it under font.family, the binaries live in tokens/fonts/, the generator writes the @font-face blocks, and two guarantees in the server's suite read the binaries themselves.
fonts.display: Vollkorn, variable wght 400-900, SIL OFL 1.1, no Reserved Font Name
fonts.text: Commissioner, variable wght 100-900 with slnt / FLAR / VOLM, SIL OFL 1.1, no Reserved Font Name
fonts.languageAttribute: The active locale must be set as a language attribute on every surface (document lang, Android LocaleList, SwiftUI .environment(\.locale) or an NSAttributedString language attribute). Without it a shaper uses the default language system and no locl substitution runs, so Bulgarian, Romanian, Turkish, Catalan and Dutch all lose their local forms.

color.$description: Primitive ramps. Every value is generated from OKLCH and carries its 6-digit sRGB fallback; the two agree exactly for all 49 steps. Primitives are never referenced by a screen: only the theme roles below are.

200.$description: Placed where the brand ramp places its own 200, on this family's curve: it is the lighter step a filled control moves to on hover in the dark theme, and the stronger tint a control takes when pressed in the light one.

800.$description: The pressed step of a filled control in the light theme, placed where the brand ramp places its own 800.

200.$description: Placed where the brand ramp places its own 200, on this family's curve.

800.$description: Placed where the brand ramp places its own 800, on this family's curve.

scrim.$description: The only entries in the palette that carry an alpha channel. A scrim is not a step on a ramp: it is one ink laid over whatever is behind it, and the two entries differ only in how much of that ink each theme needs to separate a sheet from the page under it. They live here rather than in the theme layer because a theme role that holds a colour of its own is a value with two homes, and the rule that every role is an alias has no exception for the one role that happens to need alpha.

overDark.$description: Deeper than its counterpart because the page it veils is already dark, so the same alpha would leave the sheet and the canvas nearly indistinguishable.

display.$description: Self-hosted variable serif, wght 400-900. Declares cyrl with a BGR language system whose locl reaches 24 letters of the Bulgarian alphabet, modern Greek 71/71 with real outlines, Latin Extended-A 128/128 and the eight Maltese glyphs. Carries tnum, lnum, onum, pnum and zero: with tnum applied all ten digits resolve to one advance of 550 units, which is what the tabular and code styles depend on.

text.$description: Self-hosted variable sans, wght 100-900. Declared with an explicit weight range in @font-face: without one a variable face renders at its default instance. slnt is a mechanical slant, not an italic design, so it is reachable through font-variation-settings and is never mapped to font-style: italic.

code.$description: The role that renders an ESCO code and the taxonomy version beside it. It is not monospaced and no third face is shipped: alignment comes from the display face's tabular figures, where every digit and U+2007 FIGURE SPACE share one 550-unit advance. Only the code itself belongs in this role; the words beside it are translated prose and take the text face.

type.$description: Line height is a unitless multiplier of the font size, as the format requires, and the rendered value is the multiplier times the size rounded to a whole pixel. Two floors, each derived from a measured ink extent rather than from taste. Text face: worst ink 1.290 em across the full Latin, Greek and Bulgarian inventories, floor 1.35. Display face: worst ink 1.190 em over the same inventories, taken over the Bulgarian locl alternates because those are the glyphs the BGR language system substitutes in. The measured floor is therefore 1.19; the display styles are set at 1.30, which is a chosen ratio above that floor rather than the floor itself, so that a later face with slightly deeper ink does not silently start clipping. Letter spacing is in px, exact at each style's declared size; the proportional value it comes from is kept in the token's extensions so a generator emitting sp or scaled points keeps the intent.

displayLg.$description: 40/52 px. Clears the display face's 1.190 em ink by 4.40 px.

heading.$description: 18/25 px. Set in the text face, so it takes the 1.35 floor; 25 px is the smallest whole pixel at or above it.

label.$description: 14/20 px. Never rendered through text-transform: a capitalisation applied in CSS changes what a screen reader says and mangles Greek accentuation.

caption.$description: 13/18 px. The smallest style permitted on mobile and on candidate web.

tabular.$description: 16/24 px. Salaries, dates and counts. The OpenType settings are not part of the typography composite the format defines, so they are carried in this token's extensions and must be emitted as a companion declaration on every target: one form, not two.

$extensions.bothdecks.swiftui: .monospacedDigit() is not equivalent; apply the tnum and lnum features through the font descriptor

code.$description: 13/18 px. ESCO codes, offer identifiers and verification codes, always with the taxonomy version beside them. Same tabular figures as the tabular style, so a column of codes aligns.

denseLabel.$description: 12/18 px. Recruiter console only, and the smallest style the system has.

floor.$description: The minimum rendered font size per surface, at the system font scale of 1. Below these values a style is not available on that surface; the absolute floor holds everywhere with no exception.

space.$description: Named by value in px, not by multiplier, so the name and the number can never disagree. A 2 px grid up to 20 px and a 4 or 8 px grid above it. The half-steps 6, 10, 14 and 18 are declared members rather than exceptions: a scale that half the layout has to step outside gets stepped outside again.

radius.$description: Six steps. pill is the fully rounded end cap; it is not a number a layout should ever spell out.

borderWidth.$description: Thicknesses only. The group is named borderWidth, not border, so it can never flatten onto the theme's border colour roles: border.focus is a colour and borderWidth.focus is a thickness, and a generator deriving names mechanically keeps them apart.

input.$description: functional boundaries, drawn in border.strong; a control's only visible boundary is always this one

focus.$description: focus ring, drawn in border.focus or border.focusOnFill, outward offset 2 px and 3 px on cards, never inset and never removed

dash.$description: The one dashed boundary the system draws: the chip that names a skill a candidate does not have yet. It is the second carrier of that meaning, so that the difference between a skill you have and one you do not is not left to colour alone. Written as two lengths rather than as a stroke style, for the same reason a spring is written as its members: the format has no composite the three targets read the same way, and a dash left to each of them is a dash that agrees by luck. The web draws it with a border image or an inset shadow rather than with `border-style: dashed`, whose pattern belongs to the browser and differs between them.

icon.$description: Icons are drawn on a 24 px grid with a 2 px live-area padding, round caps and joins, and take currentColor. Stroke and hit target are both groups rather than single numbers: the stroke a glyph is drawn with does not scale with the frame, because an optically even icon needs a heavier stroke when it is small, and the two platforms specify different minimum targets. One number for either would be a number that is wrong somewhere.

lg.$description: at icon.size.lg, the grid the set is drawn on

selected.$description: a selected tab at icon.size.lg; weight is the second carrier of the selected state, never its only one

control.$description: The geometry every interactive control is built from: buttons, inputs, selects, chips, switches and segmented controls. Three sizes, each tied to a surface rather than to a number, so that a control cannot acquire a fourth height by being drawn slightly differently on one screen. Height is authored rather than derived: it is not a spacing step and it is not a hit target, and expressing it as either would make a later change to one silently move the other.

sm.$description: recruiter console only, which is a pointer surface; clears the 24 px minimum target with room

md.$description: the default everywhere a finger is used, and the size of every icon-only button; equal to icon.hitTarget.ios, and padded to icon.hitTarget.android on Android without the drawn height changing

lg.$description: the emphasised action on a mobile screen, and the two deck actions

thumb.$description: The disc a switch moves. Held apart from the spacing ramp for the same reason a height is: a gap that happened to share the number would move with it the day one of them changed.

travel.$description: How far that disc moves. Position is the switch's non-colour carrier, so this distance is what makes on and off tellable apart without seeing the track colour.

box.$description: The drawn square of a checkbox and the drawn circle of a radio. Both are drawn rather than left to the platform's own control, because a native one takes a single accent colour and cannot show the indeterminate state this product needs. The 44 or 48 target belongs to the row around it, never to the 20 px mark.

elevation.$description: Four levels, each with a light and a dark form, because an effect style cannot follow a theme mode and a shadow that is only defined once is only defined for one theme. Geometry is identical across themes; the ink is neutral.950 in both, and the dark alphas are higher because the ground under them is dark. Level 0 is flat, expressed as a fully transparent shadow so the token carries a valid shadow value and can be interpolated to.

1.$description: resting cards below the top of the deck

duration.$description: Every timing the product performs, including the ones a screen would otherwise spell out as a literal. A duration that appears in an implementation and not here is a drift, not a detail.

base.$description: back transition; match crossfade; match headline

exitLeft.$description: card leaving as pass; 40 ms longer than exitRight, deliberately

snap.$description: card snapping back. This is the settle time of motion.spring.snapBack, measured at 359.2 ms, so the sampled easing ends at rest instead of being cut short.

matchHeadlineOffset.$description: delay before the match headline rises

confirmHold.$description: how long the outcome ribbon stays on screen. It overlaps the incoming card; it is never added in front of it.

advanceGap.$description: gap between one card leaving and the next becoming interactive, in both the full and the reduced path

celebrate.$description: the ceiling the whole match celebration must fit inside. Its longest path is matchHeadlineOffset plus base, 560 ms, and the matchSettle spring reaches rest at 532 ms.

snap.$description: The curve that stands in for motion.spring.snapBack where a spring cannot be run. Its peak is 1.02838, which is the spring's own measured counter-excursion of 2.838 per cent, integrated from the free release of k 400, c 30, m 1 at 400 000 samples. A linear() sampled directly from that response is carried in this token's extensions and is the preferred form; the curve here is the fallback.

$extensions.bothdecks.linearSampling: 17 uniform samples of 1 - x(t) over motion.duration.snap = 360 ms, x the free-release response of motion.spring.snapBack; the final point is clamped to 1 against a residual of 0.489 per cent, inside the spring's own settle tolerance.

spring.$description: Springs are given as a damping RATIO and a response time, which is what both native animation APIs take, alongside the mass, stiffness and damping coefficient they were derived from. A damping coefficient copied into a parameter that expects a ratio produces a spring roughly forty times overdamped, so the ratio is the value that carries the name.

reducedDuration.$description: Nothing moved, so nothing snaps. The ribbon fades out over motion.duration.reduced.

matchSettle.$description: Compose spring(dampingRatio = 0.82f, stiffness = 180f); SwiftUI .spring(response: 0.468, dampingFraction: 0.82). Reaches rest at 532 ms.

reducedDuration.$description: A fade of motion.duration.reducedCelebrate in place of the settle.
A fade in place over motion.duration.reduced.

gesture.$description: The deck's drag transfer function, so the four implementations read one value instead of agreeing by luck.

disarmThreshold.$description: hysteresis: the gesture disarms below this, so a finger resting on the line cannot chatter

flickVelocity.$description: px per second above which release commits regardless of distance

rotationPerPx.$description: degrees per px of horizontal travel

nextCardRise.$description: the resting offset of the card below, animated to zero on advance alongside its fade

theme.$description: Semantic roles. Both modes carry the same key set and every value is an alias: no literal colour is written here, so a ramp change reaches both themes at once. Where two roles in one theme deliberately share a value, the sharing is written as an alias between them rather than left to be inferred from equal hex.

sunken.$description: Wells, inputs and the bars that stand in for content while it loads. A well is told from the surface around it by its boundary and not by its fill, so the fill sits one step off the surface rather than three. What does the telling is border.strong around it, which is why every well, every input and every loading bar carries it at borderWidth.input, and why a loading bar drawn as a bare fill is the one shape in this system that disappears. A form is a column of wells; at three steps of separation it reads as a grid of grey boxes, which is a page shouting where it should be holding still.

raised.$description: In the light theme a raised surface is the card colour and its elevation is carried entirely by the shadow, because the card already sits on the lightest step of the ramp. The alias states that on purpose.

scrim.$description: The only role in the system that resolves to a translucent value. Behind every sheet, dialog and permission alert. In this theme the scrim itself does the separating: it darkens the canvas and the card by 3.10:1, and the sheet stands 3.10 to 3.20:1 clear of what it veils.

disabled.$description: Exempt from the contrast threshold under WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3, which excludes inactive controls.

subtle.$description: Decorative dividers and the boundary of a sunken well. One step stronger than the well it bounds, so a divider inside one is still visible.

strong.$description: The only value permitted on a functional boundary: every input, select and textarea, at borderWidth.input. Functional boundaries are drawn on the four neutral surfaces. A control placed on a brand or status tint takes that family's text role as its boundary instead, which clears 3:1 on every tint in both themes.

focus.$description: The focus ring on neutral surfaces.

focusOnFill.$description: The focus ring on a brand, status or inverse fill, where border.focus would sit on a surface of its own family. Which surface takes which ring is declared in the file's focusRing extension and measured by the token test.

tertiary.$description: Icons take the colour of the text they sit with; this alias names the case the audit table measures.

fillHover.$description: One step along the ramp, under a pointer. A filled control needs three steps rather than two, or hover and press look alike and a click gives no answer. There is no hover on a touch screen; this role simply never resolves there.

onInverseAction.$description: The action word in a snackbar or any other control drawn on surface.inverse.

pass.$description: Passing a card carries no hue. The roles keep the name, because a pass is a semantic thing the screens compose against, and they resolve to the neutral ramp: a pass is not a refusal, not an error and not a judgement, and a colour of its own would make it one of the three. It also leaves the interest action as the only coloured decision on the deck, so the eye is asked one question rather than two. Where the two decisions sit side by side, the interest fill against a grey pass reads for every common colour vision.

fill.$description: The pressed pass control and the pass ribbon's ink. Dark enough to carry onFill and to clear 3:1 on every surface, and the same step as text.secondary so a filled pass reads as text-weight, never as an alarm.

tint.$description: The resting ground of the pass button and of the pass ribbon. One step deeper than a well on purpose: a well is told apart by its edge and sits a hair off the page, a button is a thing to press and shows its shape. border.strong clears 3:1 on it, measured by the gate.

border.$description: The outline of the pass ribbon and the pass button, matched in weight to the interest ribbon's, which is drawn in interest.fill.

fill.$description: The full-bleed surface of the match screen.

accent.$description: The secondary mark on the match surface.

fill.$description: A 600 like every other fill in this theme, so a status mark drawn in it reaches 3:1 on every surface the design paints.

fillPressed.$description: The pressed step of the destructive action, matching brand.fillPressed one for one: a filled control that can be pressed needs its pressed colour named, or the state is invented at drawing time and differs on each of the three targets.

sunken.$description: Wells, inputs and the bars that stand in for content while it loads. The dark theme's canvas already sits on the darkest step of the ramp, so depth is read as a distinct step rather than as a darker one; this is the step that separates from the canvas, the card and the raised surface at once. It separates from the card by 1.12:1, which is why a well is drawn with border.strong around it and never as a bare fill: in this theme a bare one is not faint, it is absent.

scrim.$description: The only role in the system that resolves to a translucent value. Behind every sheet, dialog and permission alert; it still veils bright content such as an image or a light card. It cannot darken the canvas, which already sits on the floor of the ramp, so in this theme a sheet is told from what it covers by its surface step, 1.36 to 1.42:1, and by a border.subtle outline at 2.02 to 2.10:1 against the veiled background. Every sheet carries that outline; in the light theme it is optional, here it is not.

disabled.$description: Exempt from the contrast threshold under WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3, which excludes inactive controls.

subtle.$description: Decorative dividers. One step apart from every surface in this theme, so a divider on a raised surface is visible.

strong.$description: The only value permitted on a functional boundary: every input, select and textarea, at borderWidth.input. One step lighter than its counterpart in the light theme, because in this theme the same boundary is drawn on the brand and status tints as well as on the four neutral surfaces, and the lighter step is what clears 3:1 on all of them rather than on most of them: 5.12:1 on the strongest tint and 5.53:1 on the lightest surface.

focus.$description: The focus ring on neutral surfaces, and on the match surface, which is darker than the fills.

focusOnFill.$description: The focus ring on a brand, status or inverse fill. Which surface takes which ring is declared in the file's focusRing extension and measured by the token test.

tertiary.$description: Icons take the colour of the text they sit with; this alias names the case the audit table measures.

fillHover.$description: On a dark ground the three steps run towards the light, not away from it, so hover is lighter than rest and press is lighter still.

onInverseAction.$description: The action word in a snackbar or any other control drawn on surface.inverse.

tint.$description: One step lighter than the card, as the dark theme reads depth, and one step deeper than the dark well for the same reason as in the light theme: a button shows its shape.

border.$description: The outline of the pass ribbon and the pass button, matched in weight to the interest ribbon's, which is drawn in interest.fill.

fill.$description: The full-bleed surface of the match screen, drawn deep so the moment reads as its own place rather than as a tinted card. Carries match.onFill at 15.25:1.

accent.$description: The secondary mark on the match surface.

fillPressed.$description: Lighter than the resting fill, as brand.fillPressed is in this theme: on a dark ground a pressed control moves towards the light rather than away from it.
